newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian shares extend rally, Bombay up 1.55 percent.
newsitem.headline: Indian shares extend rally, Bombay up 1.55 percent.

text.p: Led by Bombay stocks, Indian blue chips powered to a strong close on Wednesday, extending the market's two-day old winning streak with shares of multinational companies topping the day's action, traders said.

"Some kind of bullishness is partly due to expectations by the investing community that the revised carry-forward report will be accepted by the Securities & Exchange Board of India (SEBI)," Alok Sethi, director at NatWest Markets, told Reuters in Bombay.
A SEBI-appointed panel on Tuesday submitted recommendations for an easier carry-forward trading system.
Hectic bidding was noticed in fast-moving consumer goods stocks (FMCG) by foreign funds and local funds, traders said.
They said newspaper reports that the U.S.'s Alliance Capital planned to float a $60-million offshore fund targeting Indian FMCG stocks led to renewed action in these shares.
"We are talking to people. If there is interest in the fund, we might take a decision next month," an official at Alliance Capital told Reuters.
Shares of Colgate rose 12.0 rupees to 317.25, Nestle gained 7.0 rupees at 293.75, Hindustan Lever added 28.50 at 1,364.25 and Ponds jumped 71.75 to 1,805.0.

Expectations that Indian markets might corner a portion of fresh investments likely to be made in emerging markets due to huge profits made by funds in booming overseas markets had also contributed to the bullish trend, participants said.
"Equities worldwide are doing well. There has been a fair bit of money finding its way into emerging markets and among Asia India is looking good," NatWest's Sethi told Reuters.
Wall Street roared to a new all-time high Tuesday after Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan delivered an upbeat view of the U.S. economy in his semi-annual report to Congress.
